//: Insolvia's brand typefaces — the ONE place they are written down, and the
companion to colors.json.
These are OVERRIDES, layered on top of the installed @insolvia-ai/tokens,
for exactly the reason the colours are. The design system's base theme
sets `heading` and `body` to the same system sans and says why:
'The base theme no longer ships a display face: heading and body are
the same sans stack, because a distinct heading family is a brand
decision and this package's default theme deliberately makes none.'
So the package leaves a seam — `ThemeProvider`'s `fonts`, and the
`--font-*` custom properties on web — and the brand is the consumer's to
state. Same bargain as ADR 0020, same file shape, same generator.
THE UI IS ONE FACE. `heading` and `body` are both Open Sans, on purpose,
and that is the decision most likely to be re-litigated here. The serif
used to be the heading face too, and a case overview then set three
families on one screen: a calligraphic serif in the card titles, the sans
in the rows under them, and mono in the figures. At the 16px a card title
actually uses, a face drawn for display sizes read as an ornament rather
than a heading, and the page had no single voice. Hierarchy inside the
app now comes from size, weight and spacing in ONE family — which is how
the platforms' own UI type works, and what every dense-UI reference
recommends. The serif is reserved for the logotype, below.
WHY THESE THREE:
Open Sans     the UI face — headings, labels, controls, body copy. Chosen
for how it reads at 12-14px in a dense table rather than
for how it looks in a heading. Humanist, with a tall
x-height and open apertures, which is what keeps a column
of creditor names and addresses legible at the sizes this
app actually sets. It replaced Public Sans, which was
picked for its provenance — drawn for the US Web Design
System, that is, for federal forms — a register this tool
works in but which the reader never sees; Open Sans is
the more widely proven text face at these sizes. Two
weights are loaded, 400 and 600: regular for text,
semibold for every heading and emphasised label. There is
no 700 — a third weight is a third download, and at UI
sizes bold over semibold adds bulk, not hierarchy.
Cormorant Garamond  the wordmark's face, and ONLY the wordmark's — the
one place the brand gets to have a voice. Calligraphic
— the strokes read as written rather than drawn —
with very high contrast and sharp pointed serifs.
Chosen as the closest shippable face to Ogg (Sharp
Type), which is licensed and could not be embedded.
It is what brand/wordmark.svg and brand/icon.svg
are cut from, and what the app's `Wordmark`
component sets at 700: Cormorant is drawn for large
sizes and is markedly lighter than the didones it
sits beside, and at anything under 700 the logotype
goes delicate. Nothing else may use this role; a
heading that reaches for it is the mistake described
above.
IBM Plex Mono case numbers, districts, form references (B106 · Schedule
D), amounts, timestamps. Anything that must align by
column or be read back to somebody over the phone. NOT
status words or labels: 'blocked' set in mono is a figure
that isn't one.
Each stack ENDS in the same generic the base theme uses, so a face that
fails to load degrades to what shipped before rather than to Times.
THE FILES ARE NOT AUTOMATIC. A family name is only a request; something
has to load the face. On web that is an @font-face rule and a .woff2 —
for this repo, self-hosted in apps/insolvia_app/public/fonts (see the OFL
notice there, and scripts/fetch-brand-fonts.sh which produces them). On
React Native it would be expo-font and a linked file, which is why the
design system ships no font binary itself.
WHERE THE FACES ARE ACTUALLY LOADED TODAY: the app, and only the app.
The marketing site and the admin portal receive the same --font-* values
from this file, and until each loads the faces itself its stacks fall
through to the system sans they already rendered. That is a stated
state, not an oversight: both are outside this workspace with their own
lockfiles and their own public directories, and neither had a typography
decision made for it here. `wordmark` reaches them too and neither uses
it — they render the SVG mark, which carries the letterforms itself.
DO NOT hand-copy these values into an app. Every consumer is generated
from this file by `npm run tokens`, and `npm run tokens:check` fails the
build when one has drifted.
heading: "Open Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace
